- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day horizon by 1–3% in early cycles; apply 1.5% downward bias for 30d forecasts.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.6, 0.2, 0.6), model fails to adjust; use moving average of last 3 sentiment values to weight forecast correction.
- If true outcome deviates >2% from 30d forecast, check if sentiment was high 3–5 days prior — if yes, reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
